description:
Give `RootRelativePath::parse` an error type of its own, move the type and that error into a pure domain module, point every importer at the domain path, delete the `repository_state` re-export, and assert that the domain layer names nothing in `repository_state`.

## Background

- `RootRelativePath::parse` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/path.rs:82-104`) returns `RepositoryLayoutError::LexicalEscape` (`path.rs:701`, message "path '{0}' is not lexically confined"), a variant of the layout error that also covers root evidence and symlinked roots. That ties the pure path type to `repository_state`.
- `?` sites whose function returns `RepositoryLayoutError` keep compiling through a `From` conversion: `VirtualPath::worktree`/`data` (`path.rs:362,368`), `RepositoryLayout::new` (`path.rs:506`), `package_tree.rs:200,356`, `ancestor_dirs` (`initialize.rs:1061`) and `gate_run_result_relative_path`'s first parse (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:510`). Sites under `anyhow` (`commands/snapshot.rs`, `commands/profile.rs:597`) and the two `to_string` mappings (`storage/json.rs:1503`, `storage/artifact_planning.rs:288`) need no change.
- Sites whose function returns another error type rely today on that type's `#[from] RepositoryLayoutError`, and a second conversion step does not chain through `?`:
  - `canonical_path` (`crates/jit/src/storage/redo_record.rs:387`, `RedoRecordError`);
  - `ensure_memory_parent_exists` (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:1323`, `RepositoryStateStoreError`);
  - `resolve` (`crates/jit/src/storage/memory.rs:628-655`, parse at `:647`, `RedoApplyError`, whose `Path` variant converts from `RepositoryLayoutError` at `crates/jit/src/storage/redo_apply.rs:84`);
  - `validate_pinned_request` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/image.rs:916`, `CaptureError`);
  - `create_ancestors` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/archive.rs:382`, `.map_err(ProducerError::from)`);
  - `tree_path` and `immediate_parent` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/export.rs:255,266`, `RepositoryExportError`);
  - `gate_run_result_relative_path`'s tail expression (`mutation.rs:514`), which returns the parse result directly.
- `ensure_ancestor_dirs` (`memory.rs:411-412`) chains the parse into `VirtualPath::from_root` with `.and_then`, which needs one error type, so it converts the parse error explicitly before the chain.
- `RootRelativePath` (`path.rs:68-146`, with `Serialize` `:148`, `Deserialize` `:157` and `JsonSchema` impls) and its parse error are pure: they read no filesystem and name nothing else in `repository_state`.
- The type uses two private helpers in `path.rs`. `RootRelativePath::contains` calls `enters` (`:49`, used at `:135`), which `is_bootstrap_lock` (`:45`) and `VirtualPath` (`:269`) also call, so it cannot move privately. The method `join` (`:140`) is private and is called from `path.rs:558`.
- `crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:9-13` imports it from `repository_state` for `ProfileOrigin::Directory` (`:1195`), with a comment defending the import. Under `@/inv/architecture-dependency-direction` the domain imports nothing from `repository_state`.
- `crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:145-150` re-exports the type from `path`, and about twenty files import it through that path:
  - repository state: `crates/jit/src/repository_state/export.rs`, `package_tree.rs`, `mutation.rs`, `materialize.rs` (`crate::repository_state::RootRelativePath` at `:638`, `:641`), `initialize.rs` (`super::path` import at `:35`), `image.rs` (`super::RootRelativePath` at `:916`), `archive.rs` (`super::RootRelativePath` at `:382`);
  - storage: `crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs` (grouped `crate::repository_state` import at `:8-14`; parse at `:1323`; its no-follow readers, such as `read_repository_file_nofollow`, take `&RootRelativePath`), `storage/memory.rs` (import `:11`, `:411`, `:647`), `storage/json.rs` (`crate::repository_state::RootRelativePath::parse` at `:1503`), `storage/redo_record.rs` (import `:12`, `:387`), `storage/artifact_planning.rs` (`use` at `:15`) while that file exists;
  - commands and gate execution: `crates/jit/src/commands/profile.rs` (grouped import `:20`, `:597`, and tests: import `:1894`, `:2346`, `:2581`, `:2585`, `:4625`), `commands/snapshot.rs` (the `SnapshotDirectories`/`SnapshotFiles` aliases at `:15-16`, `crate::repository_state::RootRelativePath::parse` at `:176`, `:213`, `:454`, `:463`, `:593`, `:600`; the reader calls beside `:176` and `:463` name `crate::storage::repository_state_store::read_repository_file_nofollow`), `commands/archive.rs` (`capture_artifact_evidence`, `:418`), `crates/jit/src/gate_execution.rs` (`use` at `:14`).
- Pure parse tests live in `path.rs`: `test_path_constructors_and_serde_reject_noncanonical_spellings` (`:917-939`, its `RootRelativePath` assertions) and `test_root_relative_path_uses_variant_not_empty_string_sentinel` (`:967-990`). `test_borrowed_const_and_owned_parse_unify_as_one_key` (`:1061`) uses `VirtualPath` and stays.
- The artifact classifier's `crate::repository_state::ProducerError` uses (`crates/jit/src/domain/artifact_classifier.rs:783,837,844,865,897` and tests `:2785,3021`) are removed by `domain-typed-errors`. Prose mentions in rustdoc (`domain/types.rs:610,1675`) name the module, not a path, and are not imports.
- The cutover scan fixture strings in `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:1336,1361` name the type as text and are unaffected. Structural scans of this kind live in that file.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/jit/src/domain/relative_path.rs` defines `RootRelativePath`, a dedicated `thiserror` parse error that names the rejected text, its serde and schema impls and the `enters` helper as `pub(crate)`; `join` is `pub(crate)`; no helper is duplicated, and the module imports nothing from `repository_state`, `storage` or `commands`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `repository_state/path.rs` and `repository_state/mod.rs` define and re-export neither the type nor its parse error; no file outside `crates/jit/src/domain/` names `RootRelativePath` through `repository_state::path`, `super::RootRelativePath` or `crate::repository_state::RootRelativePath`; each names `crate::domain::relative_path::RootRelativePath`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every listed parse site compiles against the new error type through an explicit conversion into `RepositoryLayoutError` (at `memory.rs:647` a `map_err` keeps the error in `RedoApplyError::Path`), a `From` conversion into `RepositoryLayoutError::LexicalEscape` carries the same text, and the rendered message for a rejected path is unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: `domain/types.rs` carries no comment defending a `repository_state` dependency it no longer has.
- [hard] REQ-05: A structural test in `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs` asserts that no production source under `crates/jit/src/domain/` contains a `crate::repository_state` path or a `use` of `repository_state`; it fails if either the type import or the classifier's error import returns.
- [hard] REQ-06: The pure parse tests move to the domain module and pass there, one assertion checks that a rejected parse converts into `LexicalEscape` with the input text, the `VirtualPath` tests stay in `path.rs`, and the repository-state, storage (including the redo conformance suite), command, profile and gate-execution unit tests pass unchanged.

## Decisions

- D-01: REQ-04 originally required `domain/types.rs` to import `RootRelativePath` from the domain module. ceaaf0ab (6d721625c) already removed that import, leaving only a stale defending comment; REQ-05's structural scan owns the import boundary, so REQ-04 now covers the comment alone (steward ruling, 2026-11-04).

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged: messages and exit classes stay the same, the serialized form and JSON schema are identical, and the importer edits change import paths only. `artifact_planning.rs` is edited only if the archive planning helpers have not been deleted yet.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: RootRelativePath lives in the domain with its own parse error
